options: the act of cleaning the house daily
the use of family resources to achieve family goals
the study of cooking methods only

questions.stem: Which of the following careers is related to home management?
questions.explanation: Interior decoration, catering, fashion design and dietetics grow out of home management studies.

options: Children are cared for by relatives

Members help one another in times of need

questions.stem: One responsibility of parents that contributes most directly to a child's emotional security is
options: allowing the child to do anything
giving love, attention and a stable home
leaving all care to house helps

questions.stem: A balanced meal is one that

questions.explanation: Balance refers to adequate amounts of all nutrients for the person's needs.

questions.stem: Meals for elderly people should be
options: soft, easily digested and low in fat, with adequate calcium and fibre
high in fat and very spicy

cleaned, dried and stored with moth repellent

questions.explanation: Boiling kills germs; covered storage prevents contamination.

light a match to find the leak
switch on the fan at the wall socket

questions.stem:
(a) List the four steps in the management process. [4 marks]
(b) Explain how each step can be applied by a family preparing for a naming ceremony. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: Planning, organising, implementing (controlling), evaluating (1 each)
2 marks: Planning: set goals, decide guests, budget, menu, date and venue
2 marks: Organising: assign tasks to family members, arrange materials, hire canopies and chairs, buy food items
2 marks: Implementing: carry out the plan on the day, supervise and adjust where necessary
2 marks: Evaluating: assess whether goals were met, budget kept, guests satisfied; note lessons for the future
questions.explanation: The four steps are planning, organising, implementing and evaluating. For a naming ceremony: plan guest list and budget, assign tasks, carry out the event while checking progress, then evaluate success and spending.

questions.stem:
(a) What are family resources? [2 marks]
(b) Classify family resources, giving two examples of each class. [6 marks]
(c) State four ways of simplifying work in the home. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Resources: anything available to the family that can be used to achieve its goals
2 marks: Human resources, e.g. time, energy, skill, knowledge
2 marks: Non-human/material resources, e.g. money, house, furniture, land
2 marks: Community resources, e.g. parks, libraries, hospitals, roads
4 marks: Any four (1 each): use labour-saving devices; arrange work centres properly; plan and schedule tasks; sit while working where possible; combine related tasks; use correct tools; involve family members; store items near where used
questions.explanation: Resources are means used to reach family goals: human (time, energy, skill), material (money, property) and community (parks, hospitals). Work simplification: good layout, labour-saving tools, scheduling, sharing tasks.

questions.stem:
(a) Define the family. [2 marks]
(b) State two advantages and two disadvantages of the nuclear family. [4 marks]
(c) Describe the stages of the family life cycle. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Family: a group of people related by blood, marriage or adoption, usually living together
2 marks: Advantages (any two): privacy; easier to manage resources; closer parent-child bond; fewer conflicts
2 marks: Disadvantages (any two): little help in times of crisis; loneliness; heavy load on parents; children may not learn wider kin values
6 marks: Beginning (newly married couple without children); expanding (birth and growth of children); contracting (children leave home); empty-nest/aging (couple alone, retirement) (all four stages correctly described for full marks)
questions.explanation: A family is people related by blood, marriage or adoption. Nuclear families offer privacy but lack support. Life cycle: beginning, expanding, contracting, empty nest.

questions.stem:
(a) State six factors to consider when choosing a life partner. [6 marks]
(b) Explain three consequences of indiscriminate sexual activity among young people. [6 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
6 marks: Any six (1 each): genotype; blood group; HIV status/health; character and behaviour; religion; educational background; age; family background; financial readiness; love and mutual respect
6 marks: Any three explained (2 each): unwanted pregnancy; sexually transmitted infections including HIV; school drop-out; unsafe abortion and its complications; emotional trauma; stigma
questions.explanation: Choose a partner with attention to genotype, health, character, religion, age and readiness. Indiscriminate sex risks pregnancy, STIs/HIV, dropping out and unsafe abortion.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain why a pregnant woman needs special attention in her diet. [4 marks]
(b) Name four nutrients that should be increased in her diet and give one food source of each. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: To support the growth of the foetus, build the mother's tissues and blood, prevent anaemia and birth defects, prepare for lactation (any two points, 2 each)
8 marks: Any four, nutrient with correct source (2 each): protein - beans, fish, eggs, meat; iron - liver, green leafy vegetables; calcium - milk, crayfish; folic acid - green vegetables; vitamin C - oranges, guava; iodine - iodised salt, seafoods
questions.explanation: Pregnancy increases needs for growth of the baby and the mother's blood. Increase protein (beans, fish), iron (liver, leafy vegetables), calcium (milk, crayfish) and folic acid (green vegetables).

questions.stem:
(a) State four general rules for removing stains from fabrics. [4 marks]
(b) Describe the steps in laundering a white cotton shirt. [8 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: Any four (1 each): treat stains while fresh; identify the stain and fabric first; use the mildest method first; test remover on a hidden part; work from outside of stain inward; rinse thoroughly after treatment
8 marks: Steps (any eight, 1 each): mend tears; remove stains; soak; wash in hot soapy water; rub/boil if necessary; rinse thoroughly; blue; starch if required; dry in the sun; iron with hot iron while slightly damp; air and fold
questions.explanation: Treat stains early, identify them, try mild methods and test first. White cotton: mend, remove stains, soak, wash in hot water, rinse, blue, starch, sun-dry and iron with a hot iron.

questions.stem:
(a) A family uses a 1500 W electric iron for 2 hours a day for 30 days. Calculate (i) the energy used in kWh; (ii) the cost at ₦90 per kWh. [4 marks]
(b) State two advantages and two disadvantages of cooking gas as a household fuel. [4 marks]
(c) State four ways of saving electricity in the home. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Energy = 1.5 kW x 2 h x 30 = 90 kWh
2 marks: Cost = 90 x ₦90 = ₦8,100
2 marks: Advantages (any two): clean, no smoke; quick heating; easy to control; no soot on pots
2 marks: Disadvantages (any two): risk of explosion/fire if leaking; cylinder refilling cost; needs careful handling
4 marks: Any four (1 each): switch off appliances when not in use; use energy-saving bulbs; iron clothes in batches; use natural light; avoid opening the refrigerator often; unplug chargers
questions.explanation: 1.5 kW x 2 h x 30 days = 90 kWh; 90 x ₦90 = ₦8,100. Gas is clean and controllable but can leak and explode. Save power by switching off, LED bulbs and batch ironing.

questions.stem:
(a) Name four common accidents in the home. [4 marks]
(b) For each accident named in (a), state one way of preventing it. [4 marks]
(c) State four items that should be in a home first aid box. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
4 marks: Any four (1 each): falls; burns and scalds; cuts; electric shock; poisoning; suffocation/choking; drowning
4 marks: One correct prevention for each accident named (1 each), e.g. wipe spills/good lighting; turn pot handles inward; store knives safely; cover sockets/repair frayed cords; lock away chemicals
4 marks: Any four (1 each): bandages; plasters; antiseptic; cotton wool; scissors; gloves; pain reliever; burn cream
questions.explanation: Common accidents: falls, burns, cuts, shocks, poisoning. Prevention: clean floors, pot handles inward, safe storage, maintained wiring, locked chemicals. First aid box: bandages, plasters, antiseptic, gloves, scissors.

questions.stem:
(a) What is a family budget? [2 marks]
(b) List the steps involved in preparing a family budget. [6 marks]
(c) The Okafor family earns ₦120,000 a month. They spend ₦36,000 on food, ₦24,000 on rent, ₦18,000 on transport, ₦12,000 on utilities and ₦15,000 on school expenses. Calculate the amount left for savings and state it as a percentage of income. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: A written plan of expected income and expenditure of a family over a given period
6 marks: Steps (1 each): estimate total income; list family needs and wants; estimate expenditure for each item; compare income with expenditure; adjust/balance the budget and include savings; evaluate/keep records
2 marks: Savings = 120,000 - 105,000 = ₦15,000
2 marks: Percentage = 15,000/120,000 x 100 = 12.5%
questions.explanation: A budget plans income and spending. Steps: estimate income, list needs, estimate costs, compare, adjust, evaluate. Expenses total ₦105,000, leaving ₦15,000 (12.5%).

questions.topic: Rights and Responsibilities of a Consumer
questions.stem:
(a) State six rights of a consumer. [6 marks]
(b) State three responsibilities of a consumer. [3 marks]
(c) Name three consumer protection agencies in Nigeria. [3 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
6 marks: Any six (1 each): right to safety; to be informed; to choose; to be heard; to redress; to consumer education; to satisfaction of basic needs; to a healthy environment
3 marks: Any three (1 each): read labels; keep receipts; report substandard goods; buy from reliable sources; use products as directed; avoid wastage
3 marks: Any three (1 each): FCCPC; NAFDAC; SON; NCC; NERC (accept other relevant regulators)
questions.explanation: Consumer rights: safety, information, choice, being heard, redress, education, basic needs, healthy environment. Responsibilities: read labels, keep receipts, report bad goods. Agencies: FCCPC, NAFDAC, SON.
